findings.note: All four words live in the same flower-growth domain (bulb and bud are early-stage items, flower and bloom are mature-stage items), so a player sorting the board might group bulb/bud together and flower/bloom together as 'early vs late flower words' instead of keeping conversion (bulb→flower) separate from before-after (bud→bloom).

Both halves read as 'an action undone by its opposite-direction counterpart' (add undone by remove, or remove undone by add), since undoing is symmetric, so a player could defend stock:empty::sell:fill as parallel reversal pairs. Both halves read as: "stock (an add action) is undone by empty (a remove action)" and "sell (a remove action) is undone by fill (an add action)".

notes:
Two sets flagged: set-conversion/set-before-after share the flower-growth domain causing cross-set confusion, and set-reverse's stock/fill/sell/empty admits a parallel 'opposite-direction' misreading. Swap overlapping words for ones from elsewhere in the farm/feed-store world.
- set-conversion: bulb/flower and bud/bloom (in set-before-after) all live in the same flower-growth domain, letting a solver regroup them as 'early-stage vs late-stage flower words' instead of keeping conversion separate from before-after.
  Try: Replace bulb:flower with a non-flower conversion pair from the feed-store world, e.g. wheat:flour or corn:meal, keeping alfalfa:pellet
  Or: Replace alfalfa:pellet with a different processing pair (e.g. corn:feed) and keep bulb:flower only if set-before-after's bud/bloom pair is changed instead
  Or: Change bulb to seed (seed:flower) to reduce overlap with bud, provided seed does not create a new cross-set reading
- set-before-after: bud/bloom shares the flower-growth domain with bulb/flower in set-conversion, enabling the same cross-set regrouping.
  Try: Replace bud:bloom with a non-flower before/after pair from the farm world, e.g. calf:cow or chick:hen, keeping lay:hatch
  Or: Replace lay:hatch with a different natural-span pair (e.g. sow:harvest) and keep bud:bloom only if set-conversion's bulb/flower is changed instead
  Or: Change bloom to a distinct lifecycle word pair entirely outside plant growth, such as graze paired with an early-stage counterpart, to fully separate domains
- set-reverse: stock/sell and fill/empty both admit a parallel 'add undone by remove' reading (stock:empty::sell:fill), since undoing is symmetric and not tied to a fixed pairing.
  Try: Replace stock:sell with a reversal pair whose undo-direction is less swappable, e.g. open:close (open the shop / close the shop), keeping fill:empty
  Or: Replace fill:empty with a less symmetric reversal pair, e.g. load:unload, keeping stock:sell
  Or: Reword stock to restock to anchor it as a repeated replenishing action distinct from fill, reducing the add/remove symmetry with empty
Do not change: set-item-location — no allowlisted finding touches them.

All four words sit on one lifecycle timeline, so lay:chick and hatch:hen both read as earlier-to-later moments in the same span. Both halves read as: "lay occurs earlier than chick in the lifecycle" and "hatch occurs earlier than hen in the lifecycle".
